# ZAP alert filter. Tab-separated: <rule: # NOTHING HERE GATES ANYTHING, BY DESIGN.
# ZAP runs weekly against the live site from a self-hosted runner and files a
# GitHub issue with what it found. `.github/workflows/dast.yaml` sets
# `fail_action: false`, and this file contains no FAIL rows -- those two facts
# agree on purpose, and they must be changed together.
# The reason: every rule that would be worth failing on is a header the shared
# Gateway does not set yet (there is no ResponseHeaderModifier filter anywhere in
# the repo). A FAIL row here would make the weekly cron red from its first run,
# and a cron job that is always red is one nobody reads.
# THE GATE IS scripts/tls-check.sh. It runs in the same workflow, checks the same
# four headers, and hard-fails on the things that are green today and would be
# regressions: reachability, the http -> https redirect, and certificate expiry.
# TO PROMOTE A HEADER TO A GATE, in one commit:
#   1. add the ResponseHeaderModifier filter in infrastructure/gateway
#   2. move the rule ID below from WARN to FAIL
#   3. set `fail_action: true` in dast.yaml
#   4. set STRICT_HEADERS=1 on the tls step in dast.yaml
# Only rules with a stated reason belong here. Everything not listed keeps its
# default behaviour, which for a baseline scan is WARN.
# Find a rule ID in the ZAP HTML report, or:
#   https://www.zaproxy.org/docs/alerts/
# Expected because every target sits behind Keycloak
